limitations: Static regulatory flood-hazard planning context, not a forecast of this storm or a current flood extent.
Not a road closure, bridge failure, road-level passability assessment, legal evacuation zone, or evacuation order.
Outside mapped high-hazard areas does not mean safe; rainfall, drainage and other flooding may occur outside polygons.
Whole source polygon features are retained, not clipped to case_bounds; some extend well outside the case area.
Server generalization uses maxAllowableOffset=0.000025 degrees (roughly 2.8 m latitude) and six decimal coordinates; not survey or parcel precision.
Source scale guidance is 1:12,000. Small boundaries and holes may change under generalization.
All returned source attributes are preserved verbatim, including -9999 numeric sentinel values; these are not physical negative flood depths or elevations.
Source geometry area/perimeter fields refer to source geometry, not generalized WGS84 geometry.
State PDF introductory SFHA summary lists D/X inconsistently with its SFHA_TF field definition; classification uses actual fld_zone, zone_subty and sfha_tf, not that summary.
No individual exposure or flood-zone classification is assigned to the illustrative marker.
sources.layer_description: Flood Hazard Areas for the State of Hawaii as of June 2026 - downloaded from FEMA Map Service Center 6/15/26.  For more information, please refer to summary metadata:   https://files.hawaii.gov/dbedt/op/gis/data/s_fld_haz_ar_state.pdf  or contact Hawaii Statewide GIS Program, Office of Planning and Sustainable Development, State of Hawaii; PO Box 2359, Honolulu, HI 96804;  (808) 587-2846;  email: gis@hawaii.gov;  Website: https://planning.hawaii.gov/gis.  The National Flood Hazard Layer (NFHL) data incorporates all Flood Insurance Rate Map (FIRM) databases published by the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), and any Letters of Map Revision (LOMRs) that have been issued against those databases since their publication date. It is updated on a monthly basis. The FIRM Database is the digital, geospatial version of the flood hazard information shown on the published paper FIRMs.      The FIRM Database depicts flood risk information and supporting data used to develop the risk data. The primary risk classifications used are the 1-percent-annual-chance flood event, the 0.2-percent-annual-chance flood event, and areas of minimal flood risk. The FIRM Database is derived from Flood Insurance Studies (FISs), previously published FIRMs, flood hazard analyses performed in support of the FISs and FIRMs, and new mapping data, where available. The FISs and FIRMs are published by FEMA.    The NFHL is available as State or US Territory data sets.  Each State or Territory data set consists of all FIRM Databases and corresponding LOMRs available on the publication date of the data set.     The specification for the horizontal control of FIRM Databases is consistent with those required for mapping at a scale of 1:12,000. This file is georeferenced to the Earth's surface using the Geographic Coordinate System (GCS) and North American Datum of 1983.

sources.layer_description: Street Centerlines for the Island of Oahu as of August 2024.  Source: Hawaii Statewide GIS staff downloaded from Honolulu Land Information System, September 26, 2024. Street network of Oahu, contains both non-military and military streets. Provides a foundation for routing applications and geocoding essentials used by the City's first responders. Purpose is to support common geographic and network analysis, routing and base mapping for City staff, Emergency Management, Homeland Security and Public Safety organizations.This layer includes data provided to the City by various military branches; but updates to the military streets are infrequent.To obtain the latest version of the Oahu Street Centerline layer, users should visit the HOLIS Open Geospatial Data Portal at https://honolulu-cchnl.opendata.arcgis.com/.  For additional information, please refer to complete metadata at https://files.hawaii.gov/dbedt/op/gis/data/streets_oah.pdf or contact the Hawaii Statewide GIS Program, Office of Planning and Sustainable Development, State of Hawaii; PO Box 2359, Honolulu, HI 96804; (808) 587-2846; email: gis@hawaii.gov; Website: https://planning.hawaii.gov/gis.

sources.layer_description: National Bridge Inventory Bridges in Hawaii as of June 20, 2025. .  The National Bridge Inventory dataset is as of June 20, 2025 from the Federal Highway Administration (FHWA) and is part of the U.S. Department of Transportation (USDOT)/Bureau of Transportation Statistics (BTS) National Transportation Atlas Database (NTAD). The data describes more than 624,000 of the Nation's bridges located on public roads, including Interstate Highways, U.S. highways, State and local roads, as well as publicly-accessible bridges on Federal and Tribal lands. The inventory data presented includes information on the location, description, classification, and general condition for each bridge. The Recording and Coding Guide for the Structure Inventory and Appraisal of the Nation's Bridges (Coding Guide) contains a detailed description of each data element including coding instructions and attribute definitions. The Coding Guide is available at: https://doi.org/10.21949/1519105. For additional questions regarding regulations for the National Bridge Inventory or the Coding Guide please contact the National Bridge and Tunnel Inventory team at NBTIS_Support@dot.gov. For questions on the geospatial component of the dataset, contact the NTAD team at NTAD@dot.gov. A data dictionary, or other source of attribute information, is accessible at https://doi.org/10.21949/1519105. Hawaii bridges downloaded by Hawaii Statewide GIS Program on 7/13/26 from https://geodata.bts.gov/datasets/usdot::national-bridge-inventory/about. For more information, please see metadata at https://files.hawaii.gov/dbedt/op/gis/data/bridges_nbi.pdf or contact Hawaii Statewide GIS Program, Office of Planning and Sustainable Development, State of Hawaii; PO Box 2359, Honolulu, Hi. 96804; (808) 587-2846; email: gis@hawaii.gov; Website: https://planning.hawaii.gov/gis.

backend_source_trace.difference_from_backend_display_query: This snapshot includes all A/AE/VE/X subtypes in case_bounds; backend nearby display filters sfha_tf='T' or 0.2% subtype and generalizes more coarsely. No other hazard layer is acquired here.

geometry_processing.selection: Source spatial intersects envelope in EPSG:4326; A/AE/VE/X filter for flood polygons. Park is additionally filtered to objectid 231.
geometry_processing.source_polygon_extent_policy: Whole source polygon features; use case_bounds for display framing. Full-resolution query measured 15,153,792 bytes, so server-generalized geometry was selected for compactness.
geometry_processing.other_geometry: Road/stream coordinates rounded to six decimals; bridge/park source precision retained. No invented official linework or crossing geometry.
geometry_processing.source_attributes: All fields returned by documented outFields preserved verbatim. Added properties are prefixed context_. Feature IDs are source-id:objectid.

illustrative_marker.label: Kupuna A · fictional exercise planning marker
illustrative_marker.verification: Official park point-intersects query returns Waianae District Park, objectid 231.
illustrative_marker.previous_point_status: No park intersection in this source; not verified nonresidential. No residential classification or address lookup was performed.
illustrative_marker.limitations: Inside a historical public park polygon, not verified open ground within the park; no building/amenity survey. Not a real person, home, address, pickup point or safe destination. No point-level flood classification.

flood_source_fields.objectid: State mirror feature identifier; unique only within this layer snapshot.
flood_source_fields.dfirm_id: FEMA flood-risk study identifier; 15003C is Honolulu countywide study.
flood_source_fields.version_id: Product/standards version identifier, not a map effective date.
flood_source_fields.fld_zone: FEMA flood-zone designation: A approximate 1% annual chance; AE detailed 1%; VE coastal 1% with wave hazard; X requires subtype interpretation.
flood_source_fields.zone_subty: Additional flood-zone information, including floodway, 0.2% annual chance, or minimal hazard.
flood_source_fields.sfha_tf: Special Flood Hazard Area flag: T for A/V families, F for X/D per state metadata field definition.
flood_source_fields.static_bfe: Constant base-flood elevation if supplied; reference v_datum and len_unit. Not a storm forecast.
flood_source_fields.v_datum: Vertical reference datum for supplied elevations.
flood_source_fields.depth: Mapped Zone AO depth where supplied, not observed water depth.
flood_source_fields.len_unit: Units for source base-flood elevation/depth values.
flood_source_fields.velocity: Source mapped flood-flow velocity where supplied, not observed current flow.
flood_source_fields.ar_revert: Flood zone that an AR area would revert to.
flood_source_fields.source_cit: Source citation abbreviation; not a per-feature effective date.
flood_source_fields.gfid: Source-supplied identifier; not assumed unique in this mirror.
flood_source_fields.st_area(shape): Unmodified source shape area; not recalculated for generalized geometry.
flood_source_fields.st_perimeter(shape): Unmodified source shape perimeter; not recalculated for generalized geometry.
flood_source_fields.sentinels: Null, blank and -9999 are preserved. Do not display -9999 as a physical elevation, depth or velocity.

variable_definitions.context_classification: Derived flood grouping only: high (A/AE/VE), moderate (X 0.2%), lower-mapped (X minimal), other-mapped-x (other X). Never an event probability or individual exposure.
variable_definitions.context_label: Display text derived from source identifiers/classes; not an operational instruction.
variable_definitions.road_fields: segmentid/streetid identify source segments/streets; fullname/name/propername/street_typ/display_na are source names/types/labels. No routing or closure interpretation.
variable_definitions.waterway_fields: stream_nam/trib_nam are source stream/tributary names; type/type_id and hsa_code/nhsa_code/ndar_code/hgu_code are source classification/assessment identifiers, not event observations. Other fields retained without operational interpretation.

bridge_fields.location_009: Source location description, not an address for a resident.

variable_definitions.park_fields: name is source park name; tmk is source parcel reference, park_type is un-interpreted source category code, legal_acre is reported acreage. Boundary does not establish current park operation.

scenario_separation.requirement_for_future_overlays: Keep exercise-only disruptions in a separate source/layer labeled EXERCISE ONLY — NOT A REPORTED CLOSURE. Never attribute invented disruption geometry/status to these public sources.

validation.geometry_structure_checked: Finite lon/lat coordinate ranges; closed polygon rings with at least four positions; no null geometry; unique namespaced feature IDs. Engineering/topological validity not independently certified.
